## Investigation result — 2026-09-28

Fixed in source by openai/openai#1580669, merged September 26 (`32ea4804a93c68ab8534cbfc1c988fcb4ed89344`). Linux notification audio now uses Web Audio, and the DEB no longer requires `gnome-session-canberra`. No additional packaging change or duplicate PR is needed.

The original t64 diagnosis below is superseded. The [upstream report](<https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/47563>) now explicitly says `apt install` succeeds; the demonstrated failure is `dpkg -i` with the GNOME helper absent. [Debian Policy §7.5](<https://www.debian.org/doc/debian-policy/ch-relationships.html#virtual-packages-provides>) permits versioned Provides to satisfy versioned Depends. Official Ubuntu 24.04 and Debian 13 metadata confirms the affected t64 libraries provide versioned old-name aliases on amd64 and arm64. Keeping the original names and minimum versions also preserves Ubuntu 22.04 and Debian 12 compatibility.

Validation: the existing packaged app's complete dependency expressions resolve against isolated official Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 and Debian 12/13 archives for both architectures (8/8); adding the GNOME helper also resolves (8/8). The actual Debian installer renders current control metadata with only that helper removed relative to the pre-fix metadata. A control-only dpkg fixture using Noble's real t64 Provides metadata configures successfully, fails when the absent GNOME helper is required, and succeeds after its removal. ARM64 coverage is dependency resolution using the same dependency expressions, not an ARM64 app build or launch.

Release availability is unverified: production Packages index requests returned HTTP 403. This status records the merged source fix, not confirmation that a released build contains it. No new VM/container or host package installation was needed.

---

## Summary

The official ChatGPT Linux `.deb` (v26.917.62051, amd64) cannot be installed on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS with `sudo apt install ./chatgpt_amd64.deb` because its `Depends:` field lists **versioned** dependencies on pre-t64 package names that no longer exist in Ubuntu 24.04's archive.

## Repro

1. Fresh Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS.
2. Download `chatgpt_amd64.deb` from the official apt repo.
3. `sudo apt install ./chatgpt_amd64.deb`
4. Fails with unmet dependencies (`libgtk-3-0`, `libasound2`, `libatk1.0-0`, `libatk-bridge2.0-0`, `libatspi2.0-0`, `libcups2`, `gnome-session-canberra`).

## Root cause

Ubuntu 24.04 completed the 64-bit `time_t` transition (Feb 2024), renaming several libraries:

<!-- linear:table-colwidths:400,400 -->
| Old name (in the .deb) | New name (in Ubuntu 24.04) |
| -- | -- |
| `libgtk-3-0` | `libgtk-3-0t64` |
| `libasound2` | `libasound2t64` |
| `libatk1.0-0` | `libatk1.0-0t64` |
| `libatk-bridge2.0-0` | `libatk-bridge2.0-0t64` |
| `libatspi2.0-0` | `libatspi2.0-0t64` |
| `libcups2` | `libcups2t64` |

The t64 packages `Provides:` the old names, but `Provides:` cannot satisfy **versioned** dependencies (e.g. `libgtk-3-0 (>= 3.9.10)`), so `dpkg` refuses to install.

Additionally, `Depends: gnome-session-canberra` is not part of a default Ubuntu 24.04 install and is unrelated to the app's core functionality (it's a GNOME login/logout sound helper).

## Suggested fix

In the packaging pipeline, update the control file's `Depends:` to use the t64 names for modern Debian/Ubuntu (or drop the version constraints and rely on `Provides:`), and move `gnome-session-canberra` to `Recommends:` (or drop it).

## Workaround (confirmed working)

```sh
dpkg-deb -R chatgpt_amd64.deb extract
# edit extract/DEBIAN/control:
#   - libgtk-3-0         -> libgtk-3-0t64
#   - libasound2         -> libasound2t64
#   - libatk1.0-0        -> libatk1.0-0t64
#   - libatk-bridge2.0-0 -> libatk-bridge2.0-0t64
#   - libatspi2.0-0      -> libatspi2.0-0t64
#   - libcups2           -> libcups2t64
#   - drop gnome-session-canberra
dpkg-deb --build --root-owner-group extract chatgpt_amd64_fixed.deb
sudo apt install ./chatgpt_amd64_fixed.deb
```

## Environment

* Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (noble)
* `chatgpt_amd64.deb` v26.917.62051
* `dpkg` 1.22.6

## Summary

Codex can see network failures in its restricted command environment while the user's shell can reach GitHub normally. During a requested PR review, `gh pr view` and `git ls-remote` run through Codex's restricted command path failed to connect/resolve GitHub. The user ran `git ls-remote` in their shell and it succeeded. Codex then treated its own command-environment failure as inability to verify the PR head, instead of clearly distinguishing the two environments and retrying through an available authorized path.

The user reports that their own GitHub commands have been succeeding while Codex's commands have failed repeatedly. This report concerns Codex's handling of that mismatch, not a claim that GitHub DNS was down for the user.

## Steps to reproduce

1. In a Codex session with restricted command networking, ask for a review of a GitHub PR at its current head.
2. Run a read-only GitHub check such as `gh pr view <number>` or `git ls-remote origin refs/pull/<number>/head` through the restricted command path.
3. Observe the command fail with a DNS or connection error.
4. Run `git ls-remote` in the user's normal shell and observe it succeed.
5. Observe Codex stop at its own environment's failure rather than clearly report the execution-context difference and retry through an available authorized route.

## Expected behavior

Codex should distinguish command-sandbox network failures from the user's host/network state. When a requested verification is blocked in the restricted environment, it should explain that scope and, if an authorized path is available, retry the read-only check through it. It should not characterize the user's DNS/network as unavailable based only on failures in Codex's restricted command environment.

## Actual behavior

The restricted Codex command path failed to reach GitHub, while the user's shell command succeeded. Codex stopped verification and told the user it could not confirm the PR head, requiring the user to run and paste a routine Git command.

## Additional context

There are existing reports about DNS failures in specific Codex environments, including #16782. This report focuses on the agent's failure to distinguish its restricted command environment from a working user shell and to use an available authorized verification path.

No Codex version or app build was captured during this session.

### Codex versions

- Codex desktop app: `26.915.31945`
- Codex CLI: `0.155.0-alpha.9.2`
- Subscription: Pro
- Platform: macOS

### What issue are you seeing?

A repository-local Skill can remain bound to the original checkout after the same task begins operating in a fresh linked Git worktree for the same repository.

In the observed case:

- The original checkout contained an older `.agents/skills/example-delivery/SKILL.md`.
- That older Skill required a repository entrypoint that existed in the older revision.
- The task created a dedicated worktree from the latest main revision and continued the implementation there.
- In the worktree, the same repo-local Skill had already been updated and the old entrypoint had intentionally been removed.
- Codex nevertheless continued following the Skill content loaded from the original checkout.
- It attempted the retired procedure, failed because the entrypoint no longer existed in the active worktree, and blocked the task.
- Codex later noticed that the worktree contained a newer version of the Skill, but treated switching to it as something requiring user approval.

The repository state in the worktree was internally consistent. The inconsistency was between the checkout used for execution and the checkout used as the authority for repo-local Skill instructions.

This means a stale repo-local Skill from one checkout can govern commands, file reads, and workflow decisions executed against another checkout of the same repository.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

A minimal synthetic reproduction should be possible with two revisions of the same repository:

1. In commit A, add `.agents/skills/example-delivery/SKILL.md` that instructs the agent to run `node tools/old-entrypoint.mjs`. Include that entrypoint in commit A.
2. In commit B on the repository's current main branch, update the same Skill so it no longer uses that entrypoint, and delete `tools/old-entrypoint.mjs`.
3. Keep a local checkout at commit A while main is at commit B.
4. Start a Codex App task from the checkout at A and invoke the repo-local Skill.
5. From the same task, create or transition into a linked Git worktree at commit B and continue the task from that worktree.
6. Confirm that file operations and implementation work are now targeting the worktree at B.
7. Observe that Codex still follows the Skill instructions loaded from the original checkout at A.
8. The task attempts `tools/old-entrypoint.mjs` and fails or blocks, even though the active worktree contains a newer valid `.agents/skills/example-delivery/SKILL.md`.

The key condition is that the logical repository Skill exists at the same repository-relative path in both checkouts, but its contents changed between revisions.

### What is the expected behavior?

When the effective task workspace moves from one checkout to another worktree of the same Git repository, repo-local Skill authority should move with it.

Before continuing execution in the new worktree, Codex should re-resolve repo-local Skill roots from that worktree and ensure the model-visible Skill instructions match the active checkout.

At minimum, Codex should never silently use `<original-checkout>/.agents/skills/.../SKILL.md` as the workflow authority while executing against `<worktree>/.agents/skills/.../SKILL.md` when those files differ.

If hot rebinding within an existing task is intentionally unsupported, Codex should detect the mismatch and require an explicit supported handoff or a new task before executing further. It should not continue with stale Skill instructions.

### Additional information

This appears related to, but distinct from:

- #34352, where "Continue in worktree" updates some worktree metadata while the runtime remains attached to the original checkout.
- #35152, where repository Skill enablement is keyed by absolute path and therefore changes identity across worktrees.
- #16607, where resumed threads keep a stale model-visible Skill inventory.

The distinguishing symptom here is stale **Skill content and authority**: the task is operating against one checkout while workflow instructions from another checkout continue to govern execution.

A robust invariant would be that a repo-local Skill is identified by the logical Git project plus its repository-relative Skill path, while the loaded content is resolved from the task's current effective workspace revision.

Useful regression coverage would include a linked-worktree case where the same repo-local Skill changes between two commits and an entrypoint required by the older Skill is deleted in the newer revision. After the task moves to the newer worktree, only the newer Skill must be visible and executable.

- WSL agent binary: `codex-cli 0.155.0-alpha.16.4`

### What platform is your computer?

- WSL 2.7.14.0, kernel 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2
- WSLg 1.0.73.2 (enabled, default)
- Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, bubblewrap 0.6.1, systemd enabled

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Use the Codex desktop app on Windows with the agent running in WSL2 (WSLg enabled, which is the default).
2. Set sandbox mode to `workspace-write`.
3. Ask Codex to run any command, e.g. `pwd`.

### What is the expected behavior?

The sandbox starts and `pwd` prints the working directory.

### What do you see instead?

Every sandboxed command fails before execution:

```
error building bubblewrap command: app-server socket directory has an unsupported host mount at /mnt/wslg/distro; remove the bind-mount alias or nested mount before starting the sandbox
```

`apply_patch` fails with the same error, even after write permission is granted.

### Additional information

The app-server socket is `~/.codex/ipc/ipc.sock`, which lives on the distro's root filesystem. WSLg mounts that same filesystem a second time, **read-only**, at `/mnt/wslg/distro`:

```
82 67 8:48 / /                rw,relatime - ext4 /dev/sdd rw,...
84 83 8:48 / /mnt/wslg/distro ro,relatime shared:3 - ext4 /dev/sdd rw,...
```

The pre-flight mount check treats this as a bind-mount alias of the socket directory and aborts. This mount is created by WSLg on every WSL2 install with GUI support enabled, so the sandbox is unusable on a default WSL2 setup.

Relocating the socket doesn't help, because the other user-writable locations are aliased by WSLg as well:

- `/run/user/<uid>` is also mounted at `/mnt/wslg/run/user/<uid>`
- `/dev/shm` shares a mount with `/run/shm`
- `/tmp` is on the same root filesystem

items.body:
### Codex version

Codex App 26.915.4065.0; managed app-server daemon 0.157.0.

### Platform

Windows 11 Pro, build 26200.

### What happens

Sending a message in a Git repository opens several short-lived Windows Terminal windows. Their tab titles show `git.exe`. A process trace captured four new `OpenConsole.exe` instances at a turn start. The Codex app-server daemon launched Git metadata and status commands including `rev-parse HEAD`, `remote -v`, and `status --porcelain`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open Codex App in a Git repository on Windows with Windows Terminal set as the default terminal application.
2. Send a message to start a turn.
3. Watch for transient Git terminal windows during turn startup.

### Expected behavior

Background Git checks should run without creating or focusing terminal windows.

### Root cause and proposed fix

`codex-rs/git-utils/src/git_process.rs` starts these commands through `JobObject::spawn_contained`. On Windows, the job-object spawn sets `CREATE_SUSPENDED` but does not set `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`. Its fallback clears creation flags to zero, so that path can also open a console.

Proposed fix: [JRBusiness/codex@67858bd](https://github.com/JRBusiness/codex/commit/67858bd2a4f938391fef42053ef58312a4af74bc). It combines `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` with the suspended job-object spawn and retains the no-window flag in the fallback. This is a fork commit because the repository's contribution policy does not accept external pull requests.

### Verification

- A local Windows launcher using `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` ran the same turn-start Git checks with zero new `OpenConsole.exe` or Windows Terminal processes in the watcher. The upstream patch itself has not been deployed in the Codex App.
- `just fmt` passed on the proposed patch.
- `just test -p codex-git-utils -p codex-utils-pty` passed: 63 tests on Windows.

Related: #24910 and #30345.

### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.157.0`

### What subscription do you have?

Not relevant to terminal input handling.

### Which model were you using?

Not relevant; the problem is in the TUI composer.

### What platform is your computer?

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, `Linux 6.17.0-122035-tuxedo x86_64 x86_64`, Wayland (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`).

### What terminal emulator and version are you using?

[`shitty`](https://github.com/pg83/shitty), standalone Wayland terminal, release [15](https://github.com/pg83/shitty/releases/tag/15) (`st-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`). A local script named `st` launches the installed binary. No tmux or other multiplexer in the affected session.

### Codex doctor report

Not attached; the report was not needed to identify the terminal input path.

### What issue are you seeing?

After updating to 0.157.0, middle-clicking to paste the Wayland primary selection into the Codex CLI composer no longer inserts text. The user reports that `shitty` was unchanged and this worked before updating Codex to 0.157.0. This is distinct from Ctrl+V or clipboard paste.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. On Wayland in `shitty`, select text so it is available as the primary selection.
2. Start `codex` 0.157.0 with its default TUI settings in a terminal supporting middle-click paste.
3. Middle-click inside the composer.

The report comes from an interactive user session; I could inspect the configuration and source, but could not automate a physical middle-click reproduction or run a controlled 0.156.1 comparison.

### What is the expected behavior?

The selected text is inserted into the composer, as it was before the update.

### Additional information

Installed terminal provenance: SHA-256 of `/home/ei-grad/.local/libexec/shitty` is `c302a2543dae5979adb26619362477315a9a1c0b2c5b5dba66c895eb4002caa9`, identical to the `st` member of release 15's `st-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`. `gh attestation verify` succeeded for that archive against `pg83/shitty`, with signer `https://github.com/pg83/shitty/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/heads/master`. The archive digest is `2fbeb73f3a88165ce10bab2880b42beb38de61d2f666a0079f7710bdbeea96a1`. The installed file was last modified on 2026-09-02.

The local `[tui]` configuration does not set `fullscreen_transcript`. PR #47178 changed its default to `true` in 0.157.0. In the resulting owned alternate-screen mode, `OverlayInput::Default` captures the mouse; `AlternateScreen::configure_input` enables terminal mouse reporting (`?1000`, `?1002`, `?1006`, `?1003`). The terminal's source confirms the consequence: with mouse reporting active, `VtermInput::pointerButton` sends the button event to the application and returns before reaching its middle-button `paste(true)` branch. `MouseFrontendState::protocolActive` makes Shift bypass mouse reporting. Thus Codex's new default, rather than a change in `shitty`, diverts an unmodified middle click from `shitty`'s native Wayland primary-selection paste path. Sources: https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/47178, https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.157.0/codex-rs/tui/src/tui/alternate_screen.rs, https://github.com/pg83/shitty/blob/bfe3b41cd980b425a8e30263c69d110054f09ff6/lib/shitty/vterm.cpp, and https://github.com/pg83/shitty/blob/bfe3b41cd980b425a8e30263c69d110054f09ff6/lib/shitty/mouse_frontend.cpp.

An explicit `-c tui.fullscreen_transcript=false`, `--no-alt-screen`, or Shift+middle-click may be a temporary workaround; none has yet been verified by a click test. A useful fix would preserve middle-click primary-selection paste while fullscreen transcript is active.
